Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Machine Learning

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years in analytics and data science, including 4+ years building and operating machine-learning workflows used by product and operations teams. Experienced in Python, feature engineering, forecasting, churn modelling, experimentation and production data workflows using BigQuery, dbt and Vertex AI Workbench. Delivered measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and retention targeting. Developing further production software engineering practices, including automated testing; now moving towards machine learning engineering.

EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions), Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
- Built a weekly, six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow for orders by recipe and region, using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features. Scheduled notebook jobs write forecasts to BigQuery for operations teams to use in Looker.
- Reduced forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%; the resulting workflow was associated with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
- Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model, scored weekly in BigQuery, to target retention offers to top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validation showed churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Designed and analysed approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; built a sequential testing calculator in Python and Streamlit, used by around 25 colleagues. Wrote the app and Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment on Cloud Run.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Began adding pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Present results to leadership monthly and delivered internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Performed customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

SELECTED PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal, 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep-learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project only.
- Technologies: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics, University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics, University of the Lothians | 2019

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, pytest), R (tidyverse, brms), SQL (BigQuery), dbt, Git, Jupyter, Looker, Vertex AI Workbench, Streamlit, Docker, Cloud Run
Machine learning and analytics: Feature engineering, time-series forecasting, churn modelling, A/B testing, sequential testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics, model evaluation

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise and professional CV with clear reverse-chronological structure, credible metrics and good explanation of the candidate’s transition from data science toward machine learning engineering. The Thistlebox experience is particularly effective: it demonstrates measurable forecasting impact, model-supported retention targeting, experimentation, SQL/dbt work, Docker exposure and initial automated testing. The document is also appropriately transparent about the candidate’s developing production engineering experience. Minor completeness issue: the Languages section from the original candidate information has been omitted.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings, conventional bullet points, readable text formatting and searchable technology names. Relevant terms such as Python, feature engineering, forecasting, BigQuery, dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Cloud Run, Streamlit and pytest are present. However, automated screening for this specific Machine Learning Engineer role is likely moderate-to-low because the CV does not contain supported evidence for RAG or chat assistants, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow/Kubeflow/Airflow, or explicit data ingestion pipelines. The document should not add those terms as skills because the original candidate information does not support them. It can, however, make the existing GCP and orchestration experience more explicit without overstating it.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role’s Python, feature engineering, experimentation, forecasting, batch ML workflows, GCP-service exposure and measurable business impact requirements. It also shows relevant foundations for a move into machine learning engineering, including Docker, Cloud Run exposure, scheduled notebook jobs, dbt and pytest. The main gaps are substantive rather than writing defects: the candidate has not worked as a machine learning engineer for four years, has not built chat assistants or RAG systems, has not personally deployed a model as an API, and lacks stated production monitoring, data versioning and MLflow/Kubeflow/Airflow experience. The MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics are quantitative degrees but do not directly match the listed machine learning, computer science or engineering degree preference. The candidate’s remote preference conflicts with this role’s office-first/on-site arrangement in Hamburg; the CV correctly does not misrepresent this, but the location and work-arrangement issue remains relevant to application suitability. Culture alignment is partially supported through leadership presentations, internal training, cross-functional product/operations work and ownership of analytical tools, but the CV does not need to force company-culture language.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE CHANGES:
1. In the Technical Skills section, make the supported GCP experience more ATS-visible without implying broader cloud-infrastructure expertise. Change the opening technology list to include a grouped entry such as: "GCP services: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run exposure". Keep the existing Cloud Run context in the Experience section stating that the data platform team handled deployment.

2. In the Technical Skills section, make the supported orchestration and workflow experience explicit while avoiding unsupported MLOps claims. Add a truthful entry such as: "Workflow execution: scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook jobs; dbt models". Do not add MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, model monitoring or data versioning because these are not supported by the original candidate information.

3. In the Profile section, replace "production data workflows using BigQuery, dbt and Vertex AI Workbench" with the more precise "scheduled machine-learning and analytics workflows using BigQuery, dbt and Vertex AI Workbench". This better reflects the candidate’s actual batch-scoring and scheduled-notebook experience and avoids suggesting broader production infrastructure ownership.

4. In the Technical Skills section, add the Languages information from the original candidate material as a final line: "Languages: English (native), Swahili (conversational)". This restores omitted candidate information and improves document completeness.

5. In the Data Scientist experience section, retain the transparent wording that the data platform team handles Cloud Run deployment. This is important because the original candidate notes explicitly state that the candidate wrote the Streamlit app and Dockerfile but did not personally deploy a model or service as an API.

requirements.requirement: Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
requirements.quote: BigQuery, dbt and Vertex AI Workbench

requirements.requirement: Familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines
